data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts using a checklist is more reliable because the checklist decomposes a complex heuristic into a series of independent, low-variance binary checks, neutralizing the 'expert blind spot' (over-reliance on pattern recognition that fails in edge cases).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task involves non-linear dependencies where the order of checks fundamentally alters the outcome.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is underspecified, requiring domain expertise to interpret the 'checks' themselves.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Error-cancellation through additive verification: the checklist forces the explicit evaluation of necessary conditions that an expert's intuition might skip via 'fast' System 1 processing, while the panel structure averages out individual non-expert misinterpretations of the checklist items.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
